A1.justification: Both PDFs describe IFT, with matching central formulations, experiments, and results. The complete main texts and appendices are readable, and rendered figures and tables support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original Mistral fine-tuning evaluations and Frozen Lake experiments in Section 5, Tables 2 and 4, and Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains those experiments and reports additional baseline, summarization, model, and noisy-lambda results in Tables 2–3 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: Temporal residual mixing and future-token loss accumulation already appear in v1. v3 adds Algorithm 1 and an undefined 'IFT with noisy lambda' variant. Algorithm 1 multiplies token losses by cumulative-loss weights, whereas Equation 21 presents a summed-loss objective. These discrepancies prevent reliably distinguishing a changed training procedure from expanded or inconsistent documentation.

E1.justification: v3 adds dedicated TL;DR summarization evaluation, extending the earlier question-answering and general instruction evaluations. It also uses UltraFeedback variants containing newly generated Gemma2/LLaMA3 responses and ArmoRM preference labels. The original benchmarks, ARC generation adaptation, and Frozen Lake remain.

E2.justification: TDPO and SimPO are added to both direct and sequential Mistral comparisons in Tables 2–3, substantially expanding the evaluated comparator set beyond SFT, DPO, and ORPO. Frozen Lake retains its original comparators; v3 explicitly excludes TDPO and SimPO there.

E3.justification: v3 adds Gemma-2B and LLaMA3-8B configurations and a GPT-4-judged TL;DR protocol. Frozen Lake's stated MSE target changes from policy parameters to transition matrices, although Figure 3 retains its parameter-distance title and curves; this establishes a reported metric revision, not a demonstrated rerun. Existing benchmark shot counts and chat-template usage remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C, Table 7 adds a comparison between standard IFT and 'IFT with noisy lambda,' examining a mixing-coefficient variation without specifying its noise construction. The Frozen Lake analysis and comparison of multiple-choice versus generated ARC answers already exist in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for its experiments. Figure 3 retains the same curves without uncertainty bands; the additional tables continue reporting individual scores.

E6.justification: Existing Mistral scores are retained, including IFT's 59.61 Open-LLM average, while substantial new results appear. In v3 Table 3, added SimPO exceeds IFT on direct Alpaca-Eval-2 length-controlled win rate, 20.31 versus 13.27. New entries include TL;DR, Gemma/LLaMA evaluations, and Table 7's noisy-lambda average of 60.56 versus standard IFT's 59.61. The normalized cost table is removed and concrete runtimes are disclosed.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the short IFT loss derivation with expectation-based formulations and an argument that the disturbed optimal state remains unchanged in Appendix A.2. New Appendix A.4 explicitly formulates SFT, reward-model/PPO, online/offline DPO, and IFT objectives. The original MDP definitions and Bellman argument are largely retained.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a unified MDP interpretation of alignment and IFT using one policy and positive-only data to obtain competitive alignment efficiently. The shift from RLHF to Preference Optimization terminology and the additional supporting experiments preserve the substantive scope of these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation of cumulative summation as addressing missing future-token gradient feedback during parallel computation, and states that slight SFT overfitting can impair subsequent preference optimization. It removes the earlier model-generalization limitation while retaining the limited-data scalability caveat. Most interpretations of generation performance and Frozen Lake are retained.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link, Algorithm 1, and an implementation appendix absent from v1. Appendix B specifies optimizer and training settings, lambda 0.2, decay 0.95, checkpoint selection, four A6000 GPUs, runtimes, and Frozen Lake training targets. These are substantial new disclosures, without establishing that retained experiments used changed settings.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands research positioning through discussion of RAFT, RRHF, SLiC-HF, improved ranking and negative-sample strategies, and TDPO/SimPO regularization. It also adds literature supporting the language-model background and evaluation discussion. These additions extend the substantive comparison with prior alignment research.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, rewrites substantial portions of the abstract and method explanation, and changes alignment terminology throughout. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, the SFT-to-preference-optimization comparison becomes a separate section, and limitations and appendices receive a more explicit structure.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, Table 1 moves from full-width to column-width presentation, and the benchmark tables gain comparator rows and additional task/resource columns. v3 adds Algorithm 1, a hyperparameter table, and three appendix result tables, while removing v1's normalized cost table. Figure 3 is relocated and recaptioned with its plot retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical scrutiny and reproducibility: TL;DR and additional model evaluations reduce v1's narrow validation, newer baselines reveal important performance tradeoffs, and Appendix B supplies previously missing implementation settings. The loss/pseudocode discrepancy and undefined noisy-lambda variant still limit exact reproduction, and SimPO's stronger Alpaca-Eval-2 results warrant more qualified claims. These weaknesses temper, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains.
